title: California's 12th Congressional District general election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 12th Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026, after a top-two primary on June 2, 2026, advanced two Democratic candidates: incumbent Rep. Lateefah Simon and challenger Jamie Joyce. This deep-blue East Bay district, which includes Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda, and surrounding communities, is one of the most Democratic districts in the country. Incumbent Simon, a progressive civil rights advocate and former MacArthur 'Genius' Fellow first elected in 2024, faces a primary challenge from Joyce, a technology and democracy-reform activist who authored a 650-page omnibus reform bill called the MAD Act. Because both general-election candidates are Democrats, the contest represents an intra-party choice on the direction of progressive representation for the district.
polling_note: No independent public opinion polls specifically measuring the Lateefah Simon vs. Jamie Joyce general election matchup in CA-12 were found as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Lateefah Simon
candidates.summary: Lateefah Simon is the incumbent U.S. Representative for California's 12th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A progressive Democrat and nationally recognized civil rights advocate, she is the first Muslim woman elected to Congress from California and the first member of Congress born with congenital blindness. Simon serves as a Vice Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and as a Deputy Whip for Policy, and she has focused her first term on delivering district funding, affordable housing, public transit, and criminal justice reform.

candidates.name: Jamie Joyce
candidates.summary: Jamie Joyce is a first-time congressional candidate and non-profit executive running to represent California's 12th Congressional District. She is the founder and executive director of the Society Library, a non-profit working on democratic governance technology, and previously co-launched Democracy's Library at the Internet Archive. Joyce has authored the MAD Act (Mass Accountability in Democracy Act), a 650-plus-page omnibus bill that she proposes as a comprehensive reform blueprint to address issues including government transparency, AI regulation, campaign finance, and executive branch oversight.
